new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (223 pp., SIL Acrobat Paper Capture scan, no usable text layer; the PDF's metadata Keywords 'rwo; Grammatical descriptions; 32494'), rendered PDF page 10 (printed p. 2, sec. 1.2 'Brief Overview of the Karo/Rawa Language') and PDF page 15 (printed p. 7, sec. 2 'Word Boundaries') to PNG and read the scan images directly. The quoted passage is on p. 2 exactly as reported: 'Stress in the Karo/Rawa language is phonemic and therefore non-predictable. The primary stress always occurs on either the first or second syllable. The secondary stress occurs two syllables after the primary stress. In the example below, the primary and secondary stress will be capitalized to show where they occur an…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress is lexically fixed (phonemic, not predictable) but confined to a two-syllable left-edge window: it falls on either the first or the second syllable of the word. Secondary stress falls two syllables after the primary stress (an alternating pattern rightward from the primary).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly described: 'The secondary stress occurs two syllables after the primary stress' (ga.NA.ye.Roo.te; WE.ngge.Re.ngge.re).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. No minimal pairs are given to substantiate the claim that stress is phonemic; the two examples are both 5-syllable verb forms. Rawa and Karo dialects are said to be ~97% cognate; the stress statement is made for 'the Karo/Rawa language' without dialect distinction.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the statement is in the phonological overview of the word; Section 2 (p. 7) lists 'Individual word stress and intonation' as one of the criteria for word boundaries, with intonation not further described. Examples are inflected verb forms (stems + person/tense suffixes), i.e., the phonological word including suffixes.
new_statements.identity_note: The grammar describes 'the Karo/Rawa language' as a single language with two dialects, Rawa (Ramu Valley side of the Finisterres, c. 6000 speakers) and Karo (Rai Coast side, c. 4000 speakers), ~97% cognate; data come from both. Glottolog rawa1267 = Rawa [rwo] and treats Karo as part of it (I could not confirm a separate dialect glottocode). The stress statement is not differentiated by dialect. Note Glottolog's URL for the grammar uses the old SIL id 32494; the current SIL archive entry is 23695.
